sheet_conflicts: Sheet gives 130.0 km, identical to P3937's figure for a completely different corridor -- the two rows sharing the exact same length looks like a duplication/copy error rather than two independently measured pipelines. Egypt Oil & Gas ('Assil and Karam fields on the development track') documents real gathering pipelines from the Alam El Shawish West concession's Assil/Karam gas development tying into BED-3: a 24 km 12-in line, a 12 km 12-in line, and an 11.3 km 8-in line (~47 km summed across segments) -- same order of magnitude as GulfPub's cited 70 km 'Badr el Din Field - Alam El Shawish' trace, and far short of the sheet's 130 km. Likely origin of the '130' figure: an unrelated Oil & Gas Journal CO2-EOR study describes gathering CO2-rich gas from four DIFFERENT Western Desert plants (Obaiyed, El Salam, Tarek, El Qasr) to a central point in El Salam, then piping it 130 MILES (not km) to Abu Sennan field for storage -- a different corridor entirely (El Salam-to-Abu Sennan, not BED-to-Alam El Shawish) and a proposed/study concept, not confirmed built infrastructure. Plausible the sheet's '130' for both BED spurs is a garbled echo of this unrelated 130-mile CO2 study number rather than a real measurement of either spur.
notes: Two-point candidate uses BED-3 (documented tie-in hub) and the Alam El Shawish West concession centroid; straight-line distance is only ~16 km, well under both GulfPub's 70 km trace and the ~47 km summed pipeline-segment figure from Egypt Oil & Gas -- expected, since concession-block centroids don't reflect actual routing across a ~1,075 km2 block to specific well clusters (Assil/Karam sit within, not necessarily at, the block centroid). A separate Egypt Oil & Gas piece ('Field Development back on track') independently confirms Alam El Shawish and Badr El-Din are linked by transport infrastructure (for crude oil rather than this gas spur), corroborating the two fields as pipeline-connected neighbors. On the P3937/P3938 duplicate question: found evidence these are TWO DISTINCT real corridors radiating from the BED-3 hub in different directions (P3937 west/short to BED-2, P3938 west-southwest to Alam El Shawish/Assil-Karam) -- not duplicates of each other -- but the sheet's shared, unverified 130 km length for both looks like a data error that should be corrected downward for both rows rather than treated as ground truth. Confidence: moderate -- endpoint identification and general corridor direction are reasonably corroborated by 2+ independent sources (Farmout Angel coordinates + Egypt Oil & Gas pipeline description), but exact routing/length remains uncertain.

sheet_conflicts: GEM's row is named/mapped as 'Qarun' (a real but entirely unrelated Western Desert oil JV, Apache/EGPC, ~45 km 16-in OIL line to Dahshour) -- this appears to be a mistranslation/conflation of the Arabic 'Karawan' (offshore Mediterranean gas field) with 'Qarun' (Western Desert oil concession). Re-verified independently: 'Qarun' as a Western Desert brand is real (Qarun Petroleum Company, Apache/EGPC JV near Fayoum) but has no matching 206 km / 10-in gas pipeline -- its only documented pipeline is the 45 km 16-in oil line. GulfPub's 'Qarun West - WDGP-S' 18.9 km fragment (per hint) is a separate, small Western Desert gas gathering line that does not match this row's spec either -- looks like a same-name coincidence, not the same pipeline. By contrast, the offshore DEKA/Karawan/Temsah-Concession/Petrobel/32-inch-export-tie-in/El-Gamil-plant story is corroborated by two independent English trade sources (egyptoil-gas.com, offshore-mag.com) plus the row's own existing Arabic ref (almalnews.com), and its Operator field (Belayim Petroleum Co = Petrobel) matches the DEKA operator exactly -- strong evidence the row's underlying real-world asset is the Karawan-field sealine, filed under a mistranslated/conflated name. Separately, the sheet's 206 km / 10-in length looks implausible: Karawan field is only ~60 km offshore and the DEKA feature states the project laid a maximum of ~13 km of new small-diameter sealine plus tie-ins to the existing 32-in network -- 206 km does not reconcile with that description and should be treated as an unresolved, low-confidence figure (possible transcription/decimal error, e.g. 20.6 km) pending a second independent source.
notes: GEOGRAPHY CONCLUSION: independently re-verified via fresh search ('Qarun Gas Pipeline' Egypt, 'Qarun Petroleum' gas pipeline, WDGP Qarun, Western Desert Qarun gas evacuation) plus re-checking the Karawan/DEKA thread -- concluded the row's real identity is the offshore DEKA/Karawan sealine, not a Western Desert Qarun line (see sheet_conflicts for full reasoning). Could not source a precise wellhead coordinate for Karawan itself from any independent source; used the documented 'Temsah' field entry (same concession) as a concession-area start anchor, and Port Said (Wikipedia) as a named shore anchor for the export tie-in end. Both anchors are corroborated as being in the right offshore-Mediterranean-near-Port-Said geography by 2+ independent sources; the exact coordinates themselves each come from a single geocoding source. Length (206 km) remains an open, likely-erroneous, single-sourced figure -- flagged, not resolved.

sheet_conflicts: Sheet length is 38.0 km. The only literal, well-documented, geocodable place named 'Badr El Din' (the BAPETCO flagship BED oil/gas complex near Abu Gharadig, Matrouh governorate) is ~159 km great-circle distance from the derived Faramid/East Obayed start point -- a 4x mismatch that cannot be a 38 km pipeline. This means 'Badr El Din Company' in the sourcing (Egypt Oil & Gas: 'extending another line from the Faramid field to Badr El Din Company to process 24 mcf/d') most plausibly refers to BAPETCO the corporate operator (whose name derives from its Badr El Din field), not the distant Badr El Din facility itself. BAPETCO's own concession list separately includes Badr el Din, North East Abu Gharadig, Obaiyed, Sitra, and Matruh as distinct concessions, and a 'BAPETCO Obaiyed Gas Plant' facility in Marsa Matrouh Governorate was referenced (bizmideast.com) -- geographically consistent with a 38 km tie-in from Faramid -- but that page returned HTTP 403 on url_verifier and direct fetch, so its content/coordinates could not be independently confirmed and it is NOT included as a cited source.
notes: Start point corroborated by 3+ independent outlets (Rigzone, NSEnergy, World Oil, plus a Zacks search snippet) describing the Faramid South discovery as sitting in the East Obayed concession, ~30 km NW of the Meleiha concession -- consistent with the prior_suggestion. Coordinate is a computed offset from the geocoded village of Meleiha (OSM), so concession-scale, not wellhead-precise. End point: the pipeline-connection claim itself (Faramid -> 'Badr El Din Company', 24 mcf/d, matching the sheet's implied ~24-25 MMcf/d) is directly and independently sourced (Egypt Oil & Gas, citing Agiba Petroleum/EGAS investment plans) so the NAME is solid, but the corresponding PHYSICAL location is ambiguous -- the only citable, geocodable 'Badr El Din' place is BAPETCO's namesake field/complex near Abu Gharadig, which is geographically incompatible (159 km) with a 38 km pipeline from Faramid. The likelier physical destination is a nearer BAPETCO-operated facility in the Obaiyed/Matrouh concession cluster (same company, same corporate branding), but no verifiable, url_verifier-passing public source could pin down that facility's precise location within the research budget available. Set resolved:false and flagged for a follow-up pass focused specifically on locating BAPETCO's Obaiyed-area gas plant/tie-in point (try BAPETCO/Shell Egypt annual reports, EGAS concession maps, or imagery around the Meleiha/East Obayed cluster for a labeled gas facility) before drawing a two-point route -- a route to the distant Abu Gharadig Badr El Din point would misrepresent the pipeline's actual geometry by roughly 4x.

start.name: NORPETCO North Bahariya Concession (Abrar/Ferdaus/Ganna/Rawda/Rayan fields), Western Desert, Egypt
start.coord_basis: No individually geocodable point found. North Bahariya Concession (165 sq km lease awarded to NORPETCO 27 Oct 2004) sits onshore the Abu Gharadig Basin in the Western Desert, roughly 190 km SW of Cairo, between El Fayoum and the Qattara Depression. Its constituent fields (Abrar, Abrar South, Ferdaus, Ganna, Rawda, Rayan) are common Arabic words with no dedicated GeoNames/OSM entries distinguishable from unrelated places of the same name -- checked GeoNames and OpenStreetMap/Nominatim for each field name plus 'North Bahariya' with no reliable match, so no coordinate is asserted for this end.

end.name: Abu Gharadig (Abu El-Gharadig oilfield), Matruh Governorate, Western Desert, Egypt
end.coord_basis: GeoNames gazetteer entry 'Abu al Gharadiq', feature type oilfield, Matruh Governorate, Egypt (29 55'00"N 28 00'00"E).

notes: Strong corroboration for the corridor and length, weak for exact endpoints. Egypt Oil & Gas (FY2024/25 results article) reports NORPETCO 'extended a 27 km gas pipeline between NORPETCO's and Khalda Petroleum's fields' at $3.8M cost, enabling gas-for-diesel substitution and ~$12M/yr savings -- the 27 km figure exactly matches the sheet's sheet_length_km=27.0, and this is almost certainly the pipeline in question (a second outlet, African Peace Magazine, republishes the same underlying facts -- likely not fully independent of the original press release, so treat as one primary event corroborated by a re-report, not two independent investigations). Khalda Petroleum (APA/Sinopec JV) operates the 'Abu El-Gharadig Complex' field (offshore-technology.com), which is the natural referent of 'Abu Gharadig' in the pipeline name -- this rules in the hypothesis and rules out the GulfPub Abu Qir (coastal/Alexandria-area) match per the hint. NORPETCO (North Bahariya Petroleum Company) operates the North Bahariya Concession, an eastern extension of the Abu Gharadig Basin with six fields: Abrar, Abrar South, Ferdaus, Ganna, Rawda, Rayan (egyptoil-gas.com). Neither article names which specific NORPETCO field or which specific Khalda facility the pipeline physically ties into, and none of the individual NORPETCO field names could be geocoded to a distinct, verifiable point (GeoNames/OSM checks came up empty or matched unrelated places). The Abu Gharadig end is anchored to the GeoNames 'oilfield' point for Abu al Gharadiq (29.917N, 28.0E) -- a plausible but not pinpoint-precise stand-in for Khalda's Abu Gharadig Complex specifically. Given no verifiable coordinate could be established for the NORPETCO-side endpoint, resolved is set to false; a human should use this corridor (NORPETCO North Bahariya fields <-> Khalda's Abu Gharadig Complex, ~27 km apart in the Abu Gharadig Basin/Western Desert) plus internal facility knowledge (e.g. specific NORPETCO field production facility coordinates, if GEM has them) to finalize the start point.
